During the time Jesus lived, Israel was filled with people who spoke Latin, Greek (the Romans), Hebrew (Jewish leaders), and/or Aramaic. Though Jesus' native tongue was Aramaic, scholars speculate that Jesus understood Greek but couldn't speak it. So when he taught at the Sermon of the Mound, or educated his disciples, he spoke in Aramaic. Today, this causes many problems because Aramaic is known as a language that uses exaggerated verbiage such as hyperbole and metaphors. (The same with Hebrew.) Add to that the use of idioms from that time and we have a recipe for many misunderstandings.

If that isn't problematic enough, there's even more room for misconstrued understanding when you consider that even Jesus' own disciples had a hard time understanding him.
